report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Strong clinical trial evidence demonstrates that abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

### Summary of Evidence
* **Clinical Trial Findings**: In the pivotal Phase 3 ACTIVE (Abaloparatide Comparator Trial In Vertebral Endpoints) randomized clinical trial, postmenopausal women with osteoporosis receiving daily subcutaneous injections of abaloparatide (80 µg) experienced a statistically significant reduction in new morphometric vertebral fractures over 18 months compared to those receiving a placebo.
* **FDA Approval**: Based on data from the ACTIVE trial and its extension study (ACTIVExtend), the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved abaloparatide (brand name Tymlos) in 2017 specifically for treating postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture, citing its proven efficacy in reducing both vertebral and nonvertebral fractures.

### Sources
* **JAMA Clinical Trial**: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640
* **FDA Prescribing Information**: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf
* **ACTIVE Trial Summary**: https://www.healio.com/news/endocrinology/20160816/active-abaloparatide-reduces-fracture-risk-in-postmenopausal-women-with-osteoporosis
* **FDA Approval Overview**: https://www.managedcaremag.com/news/fda-approves-tymlos-osteoporosis-postmenopausal-women/
